headline.purpose: Big section statements: Results, Platform, Close.

title.purpose: Bento tile and step titles; FAQ questions at 500.

lead.purpose: The line under each heading, Slate, 30-34rem measure.

body.purpose: Tile lines, step text, FAQ answers, footer line.

ui.purpose: Inter inside rebuilt product screens only; 12px chips, segmented controls, tabs.

ui-body.purpose: Product UI row text, panel copy, list items and in-product buttons (13px).

ui-caption.purpose: Product UI metadata, timestamps and secondary lines (11px).

ui-micro.purpose: Smallest product UI counts and labels in dense panels (10px).

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Hover color shifts, word reveals.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: FAQ icon rotation, counter flips.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: Nav state, FAQ expand, switches.

motion.name: duration-slower
motion.purpose: Entry rises and event reveals.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default entry easing (GSAP expo.out).

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: CSS state transitions.

motion.name: entry-trigger
motion.purpose: Scroll point where a section plays once; 70% for funnel and steps.

motion.name: hero-tilt
motion.purpose: Hero shot flattens with scroll; 5deg below 640px.

motion.name: motion-cursor-follow
motion.purpose: home page contextual cursor pill trail; fine pointers only.

motion.name: motion-magnetic
motion.purpose: home page nav CTA and demo-form submit.

motion.name: motion-tilt
motion.value: perspective 1400px, max 6deg (4 on hero/bento), quickTo 0.7s; depth n x 10px, 0.8s
motion.purpose: home page data-tilt / data-depth cursor tilt and layer parallax.

motion.name: motion-scroll-depth
motion.value: y -s*90px -> +s*90px, scrub true, top bottom -> bottom top
motion.purpose: home page data-speed drift, 768px and up.

motion.name: motion-scrub
motion.purpose: home page reversible scroll-tied motion: hero reassembly, results, interview zoom, how track.

motion.name: motion-reveal
motion.purpose: home page triggered heading and intro entries; 4s failsafe.

motion.name: motion-spring-home
motion.purpose: home page missed drag returns home.

motion.name: motion-spring-land
motion.purpose: home page slow drag release into its target.

motion.name: motion-throw
motion.value: InertiaPlugin, own velocity, exact end; threshold 250px/s
motion.purpose: home page thrown drag lands on target.

motion.name: motion-hold-to-drag
motion.purpose: home page touch drags never trap vertical swipes.

motion.name: motion-pin-query
motion.purpose: home page pins only here; refreshPriority in DOM order (results 3, interview 2, how 1); ScrollTrigger.sort on refreshInit.

motion.name: motion-canvas-dpr
motion.purpose: home page canvas performance cap.

motion.name: fluid-root
motion.value: clamp(16px, min(16px + (100vw - 1280px) * 0.01, 100svh / 45), 28px) from 1280px under html[data-fluid]; 16px below
motion.purpose: Every page passes `fluid`; rem type, spacing and mockups keep proportion on any desktop.

motion.name: scale-to-fit
motion.value: zoom: var(--fit), factor <= 1; width floor 0.8, height floor 0.5 with --fit-constrain: 1; fires novara:fit
motion.purpose: Shrink-only mockup fit; novara:fit refreshes ScrollTrigger. Never on Draggable or Flip scenes.

motion.name: gap-free-queries
motion.value: max query = min - .02px (1023.98px), or not all and (...); no range syntax
motion.purpose: Paired breakpoints leave no fractional-px gap.

motion.name: pin-query
motion.purpose: the interview lab pins only here; header stays inside the pin.

motion.name: ghost-pointer
motion.value: 1.25rem circle, text-primary, 2px white ring, shadow-sm, opacity 0.85; glide expo.out ~1.1s; press scale 0.85 for 120ms
motion.purpose: Auto demos: play once, cancel on real input and restore, no events in reports or live regions, skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: ambient-presence
motion.value: one step at a time; on pointer or focus finish the step and settle; resume 2000ms after leave; pause off screen (IntersectionObserver)
motion.purpose: Interactive tiles loop quietly and yield to the visitor. Off under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
A white page with one centred 1200px column, framed full-height by two 1px hairlines and cut into sections by full-width hairlines. Inside that frame the page is quiet: Geist in near-black, semibold headings with tight negative tracking, and plenty of air. The product carries the visual weight. Every section's image is the rebuilt Novara app in Inter, set on a pale plate, and it animates once to show the feature working.

The density is low and the rhythm even. Sections alternate between white and the pale gray plate (#F9FAFB), so the page reads as a stack of ruled bands, not floating cards. Violet is rare. It marks actions (buttons, focus, caret, selection) and data (funnel bars, the hired bar, chart bars, active states inside the product UI). The brand gradient appears exactly once, as a masked horizon glow behind the hero product shot.

This system documents the home page (`/`). It is hands-on: every feature can be touched, dragged, toggled or tested, and a layer of pointer and scroll interaction sits on top of the quiet frame (see Interaction layer and Motion).
keyCharacteristics: One 1200px column framed by border-secondary hairlines, with a hairline at the top of every section.
White and #F9FAFB bands alternate, and there are no section backgrounds beyond those two.
Geist for the page and Inter for the product UI. The two never swap roles.
Violet only on actions and data, and the gradient only once.
Product UI as the imagery: real text, live counters, no illustrations or stock imagery.

rules.name: The Actions-and-Data Rule
rules.body: Violet appears on things you can press and on numbers that matter. It never fills a section, a heading or decorative shape.

rules.name: The One Horizon Rule
rules.body: The brand gradient is used once per page, masked, behind product UI. Never behind text and never on a button.

rules.name: The Tint-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Status color is a 10% tint with a dot and dark text, so contrast stays above 4.5:1.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Geist speaks for the page and Inter speaks for the product. Don't set marketing copy in Inter or product UI in Geist.

rules.name: The Product Scale Rule
rules.body: Inside product UI, text sits on the 10, 11, 12 and 13px Inter steps. These sizes belong to the product; they are not exceptions to the page ramp.

rules.name: The Single Weight Rule
rules.body: Headings are always 600 with negative tracking. Hierarchy comes from size and color, never from adding bold or light weights.

rules.name: The Flat Page Rule
rules.body: Marketing surfaces (sections, plates, bento tiles, the FAQ) never cast shadows. Only product UI is lifted.

rules.name: The One Verb Rule
rules.body: A cursor pill says one verb for the one thing that element does. Elements without an action have no pill.

rules.name: The Interruptible Rule
rules.body: Every pointer-driven motion is a quickTo or a killable tween, so a new input always overrides the last one mid-flight.

rules.name: The Root-Grows Rule
rules.body: The fluid root grows everything. Nothing else scales, so nothing scales twice.

rules.name: The Gap-Free Query Rule
rules.body: Paired breakpoints are written as .98px complements or not all and (...), never as range syntax.

rules.name: The Show Once Rule
rules.body: An auto demo plays one time, yields to the first real input, restores the state it changed, and leaves no trace in reports or live regions.

rules.name: The Yield-to-Presence Rule
rules.body: An ambient loop never runs under a visitor's pointer or focus. It finishes its step, settles, and resumes only after they leave.

rules.name: The Header-in-Pin Rule
rules.body: A pinned scene pins its heading with its steps. The visitor never scrubs through a step without the line that names it.

rules.name: The Two-Surface Rule
rules.body: Integrity UI never appears on the candidate's surface. It lives only in the team's view, and a pulse is the only thing that crosses between them.

dos: Do keep every section inside the 1200px hairline-framed column, with a full-width top hairline.
Do alternate white and Plate Gray (#F9FAFB) bands, and only those two.
Do show features as rebuilt product UI in Inter on a plate, with real text and a screen-reader caption.
Do keep violet to actions and data, and make the final or most important bar the only full-strength one.
Do set headings in Geist 600 with -0.03em tracking and balanced wrapping.
Do play triggered motion once, on entry, with expo-out, and leave every end state visible without JS or under reduced motion.
Do give each home page element one motion kind (scrubbed, triggered or interactive), and make scrubbed motion fully reversible.
Do opt into the home page interaction layer with data attributes (`data-cursor`, `data-magnetic`, `data-tilt`, `data-depth`, `data-speed`), and give every drag a button or keyboard equivalent.
Do set product-UI text on the 10, 11, 12 and 13px Inter steps.
Do author page and mockup sizes in rem under data-fluid.
Do write paired breakpoints as .98px complements or not all and (...).
Do keep a pinned scene's heading inside the pin, and leave the first and last steps free of snapping.
Do cancel an auto demo on the first real input, restore what it changed, and play it only once.
donts: Don't use the brand gradient anywhere but the single hero horizon, and never behind text.
Don't put shadows on marketing surfaces. Shadows are for product UI.
Don't fill status chips with full-strength color. Use the 10% tint, a dot and dark text.
Don't pin below 768px wide or 620px tall, and never trap vertical swipes on touch.
Don't add a cursor pill to an element that does nothing, or run pointer effects under reduced motion or on touch (except the idle drift).
Don't introduce colors outside the token palette. The palette is binding.
Don't use range media syntax (width < 1024px), px text inside a rem mockup, or zoom on a Draggable or Flip scene.
Don't let demo or ambient events reach a report, a live region or the clipboard, or run them under reduced motion.
Don't put integrity UI on the candidate's surface, or show a slot confirmation as an overlay.
